technical.lead: GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna reach GA across ChatGPT, Codex, and the API
technical.body: OpenAI moved the GPT-5.6 family to broad availability on July 9 with a three-tier price ladder: Sol at $5/$30 per million tokens for frontier reasoning and agentic work, Terra at $2.50/$15, and Luna at $1/$6 for high-volume pipelines. GitHub Copilot enabled all three tiers the same day.

citations.label: OpenAI - GPT-5.6: Frontier intelligence that scales with your ambition
GitHub Changelog - GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna available in Copilot

technical.lead: GPT-5.6 adds max reasoning effort and a subagent-driven ultra mode
technical.body: Beyond the price ladder, the GPT-5.6 release introduces a max reasoning effort setting that gives Sol its longest thinking budget and an ultra mode that fans complex tasks out to subagents, pushing the product line toward orchestrated multi-agent execution rather than single-model calls. Terra matching GPT-5.5-class performance at roughly half the cost also resets the mid-tier floor competing frontier APIs price against.

citations.label: OpenAI - GPT-5.6: Frontier intelligence that scales with your ambition

technical.lead: Meta opens its first paid Meta Model API with Muse Spark 1.1
technical.body: Meta Superintelligence Labs released Muse Spark 1.1 on July 9 — a multimodal agentic model with a one-million-token context window — and, for the first time, is charging for access ($1.25/$4.25 per million tokens) via a public preview of the Meta Model API. The model posts leading tool-use scores (88.1 MCP Atlas, 54.7 JobBench), entering the frontier market below every competing flagship tier.

technical.lead: Microsoft scales MDASH agentic scanning to the full Windows codebase
technical.body: Microsoft announced on July 9 that MDASH — a multi-model harness orchestrating over 100 specialized AI agents to discover, debate, and prove exploitable bugs — is moving onto dedicated cloud infrastructure sized for Windows-scale scanning. It has already surfaced 16 vulnerabilities in the networking and authentication stack, including four critical RCEs in components like the kernel TCP/IP stack and the IKEv2 service, and Microsoft argues the industry must shift from calendar-bound patching to continuous, risk-driven remediation.

technical.lead: ICML workshops close July 11; Hot Chips early rate ends July 31
technical.body: ICML 2026 in Seoul wraps its workshop program July 10-11, making tomorrow the last day to catch sessions. The next hard deadline is the Hot Chips 2026 early-registration rate, closing July 31 ahead of the August 23-25 conference at Stanford, while the August security block — the AI Risk Summit (August 11-12, Half Moon Bay) plus Black Hat USA and DEF CON 34 in Las Vegas — and Ai4 (August 4-6, Las Vegas) are the next dates to book.
